messages.subject: Re: Importing Latex tables
messages.body_plain:
Consider two options: (1) produce html directly with the htmlTable package in R or (2) use HeVeA (http://hevea.inria.fr/) which does a nice job converting to html.
Frank

messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Importing Latex tables
messages.body_plain:
Yes and no. Technically rmarkdown passes anything it does not understand on to whatever comes after rmarkdown. If you have chosen to make pdf output then the next step is a LaTeX processor, and simply including it in the text of your document will work. On the other hand, if you produce html or docx, the LaTeX code will not make sense.

I happen to think using knitr WITHOUT rmarkdown (raw LaTeX with r blocks) is more straightforward if you want to build something as ambitious as a thesis... but other people have different opinions on this.

messages.subject_clean: CSS style for span classes in code chunks
messages.body_plain:
Hi everyone,

I'm working on a presentation with R and knitr, and I would like to specify my own CSS style.

I use an external custom.CSS file as described in the begining of my .Rmd file :

output:
  slidy_presentation:
    css: custom.css
    highlight: espresso
  beamer_presentation: default
  ioslides_presentation:
    highlight: espresso
    smaller: yes
transition: rotate

Some styling is applied, but I can't figure out how to apply styling to the different classes of span used in the code chunks. When I examine the page in the browser, I can see the calsses names, but can someone tell me how to style them in my custom.CSS file ?

Best

Mathieu

messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Existing Rmd file to Notebook?

You are thinking of the RStudio v1.0 display feature, not a feature of knitr. AFAIK any rmarkdown file (with the YAML header) will be displayed as if it were a notebook in RStudio v1.0, but a definitive answer would have to come from RStudio support.

messages.subject: Re: [knitr] Existing Rmd file to Notebook?
messages.body_plain:
Hi
I use the following YAML header from a RStudio webinar on Notebooks with R Markdown (https://www.rstudio.com/resources/webinars/introducing-notebooks-with-r-markdown/):
---
title: "My Title"
output:
  html_notebook: default
  html_document:
    highlight: textmate
    theme: spacelab
    toc: yes
---

Then if you want to create an HTML, PDF, or Word docx file you select “Knit to HTML/PDF/Word” within RStudio v1.0 instead of “Preview Notebook”.

Emilio

messages.body_plain:
While running the scripts given below in R studio, it is nicely working. But I get the error message as"Quitting from lines 11-14 (analysisNEW_1_.Rmd)
Error in file(file, "rt") : cannot open the connection
Calls: <Anonymous> ... withCallingHandlers -> withVisible -> eval -> eval -> read.table -> file
Execution halted" when I go for File>publish.
How to resolve it?

---
title: "Augmented block"
author: "Sarma, R.N."
date: "December 21, 2016"
output: word_document
---

###Reading...

```{r}
library(agricolae)
A<-read.table("data-1.txt",header = TRUE)
str(A)
```

###Analysis by groups

```{r,echo=FALSE}
options(digits=2)
attach(A)
out<-DAU.test(BLOCK,Genotypes,HI, method=c("lsd"), console=TRUE)
detach(A)
names(out)
print(out$means)
print(out$groups)
```

###All comparison

```{r,echo=FALSE}
attach(A)
out<-DAU.test(BLOCK,Genotypes,HI, method=c("lsd"), group=FALSE)
detach(A)
names(out)
head(out$comparison)

The error Error in file(file, "rt") : cannot open the connection means R cannot find and open the file data-1.txt. You might need to include more information about the location of the file, such as ../data/data-1.txt.

Emilio
